implementation_notes: Testing is a language feature: annotate a function with #[test] (conventionally inside a #[cfg(test)] mod tests) and run it with cargo test, using the std assert!, assert_eq! and assert_ne! macros for the assert beat - the book describes a test body as setting up data, running the code and asserting the result. What replaces the xUnit fixture class is a plain function plus module organisation, with constructor helpers or a table of cases for the arrange beat and RAII Drop for teardown; a test returning Result<(), E> can propagate setup errors with ? instead of asserting on them.
pitfalls: assert_eq! needs Debug on both operands, so a type without #[derive(Debug)] fails to compile inside the macro and the error surfaces in the assert beat.
#[should_panic] asserts only that a panic occurred, not which one - an earlier unrelated panic makes the test pass.
Tests run in parallel threads by default, so helpers that mutate environment variables, the working directory or other process state break test independence unless serialised.
